justification_text:
My probabilistic forecast set the point estimate at 108.42 across all horizons—one day, one week, and one month—primarily driven by an assumption of stability in the immediate term. This suggests that based on the available information at the time of the forecast, there was no strong signal for a significant upward or downward movement. Essentially, the forecast anchored to the most recent observed value, projecting a continuation of the current state without any immediate catalysts expected to drive a substantial directional change in the short to medium term.

The width of the confidence intervals, however, progressively increased with each longer horizon, reflecting the escalating uncertainty inherent in forecasting future events. For the one-day forecast, the relatively narrow interval of [106.73, 110.11] assumed that daily fluctuations would likely remain contained, influenced by typical market noise or minor intra-day adjustments. As the horizon extended to one week ([104.65, 112.19]) and especially one month ([100.89, 115.95]), the intervals widened considerably. This broadening accounted for the cumulative effect of more variables coming into play over time, such as shifts in overall market sentiment, the release of new economic data, company-specific announcements, or broader geopolitical developments, all of which introduce greater unpredictability.

Specific risks or unforeseen events could certainly push actual outcomes outside these stated 90% confidence intervals. Such "tail events" typically involve unexpected and impactful developments that fundamentally alter prevailing conditions. For instance, a sudden and severe macroeconomic shock, like an unanticipated interest rate hike or a rapid onset of recession, could trigger a sharp market correction. Similarly, significant geopolitical crises, major technological disruptions, or unforeseen natural disasters could introduce volatility far beyond the anticipated range. Any major, unpredicted news — whether positive or negative — that significantly impacts underlying fundamentals or market psychology could lead to an outcome landing well outside the forecasted boundaries.
